newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBS HIGHER, BOOSTED BY BUYING OF LONG-TERM BONDS.
newsitem.headline: JGBS HIGHER, BOOSTED BY BUYING OF LONG-TERM BONDS.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was higher by midday on Thursday, as it received a boost from buying of long-term and super long cash bonds, traders said.
"Judging from the over-the-counter activity we are seeing, and talk in the market, it seems investors have gradually begun to buy cash bonds," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
The September is heavy at around 126.70, where a number of resistance points are located, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.

"If the September manages to break above 126.70, we may see a try for 126.91. But some market players are still stuck with long positions on the upside, which is likely to help temper rises," the second trader said.
An International Monetary Fund (IMF) report saying it would likely be desirable for Japan to begin raising interest rates later in the year had little impact on JGBs, traders said.

"There was little effect because the IMF said that while a rise in Japanese interest rates is desirable over the medium-term, they also said Japan should keep interest rates low for the time being," a foreign brokerage house trader said.
The outlook for the Japanese economy is still too weak to warrant a rise in interest rates, traders said.

"There are reports that beer shipments have gone down, along with demand for summer clothing due to poor weather. Car sales are sluggish. Taking such factors into account, a rise in interest rates is not very likely," the third trader said.

The IMF said in a report released on Wednesday: "Directors believed that the current easy stance of (Japan's) monetary policy should be maintained for the time being, but that it would likely be desirable to begin tightening later in the year."
JGBs rose early in the morning due to a rise in U.S. Treasury bonds overnight and extended gains in late morning due to buying of cash JGBs, traders said.
In the last few days, some investors have been buying the 195th 10-year bond which had been unloaded by a different investor earlier in the week, the first trader said.

"A large institutional investor had been detected shortening the duration of its portfolio earlier in the week, selling the 195th 10-year bonds and replacing them with bonds with shorter maturities," he said.
